title: i18n: `_views.VIEW.description` is declared, walked and counted as covered but never rendered — plus three surfaces a bundle cannot address at all
body:
Filed from an app repo (`objectstack-ai/hotclm`, `@objectstack/*` 17.3.0, `@objectstack/console` as shipped) after translating it end to end into `en` + `zh-CN` — `objectstack-ai/hotclm#32`, PR `objectstack-ai/hotclm#33`. ⛔ Unassigned, ungraded; routing is triage's.

**Four findings, filed together because they are one seam** — the gap between what the i18n coverage walk *addresses* and what the console *renders*. **Finding 1 is the serious one** and would justify its own card; the other three are the same seam in its benign direction (nothing to address, so nothing claims coverage). Split if triage prefers.

**Provenance.** All four were measured in a browser by the card-11 implementation run, each with a stated repro. I reviewed the evidence and the reasoning and merged the PR on it; I did not personally re-drive these four, and I say so rather than implying otherwise. (I did independently re-measure a *fifth*, unrelated finding from the same run and found it inverted — see `#16695` — so these are not offered as unexamined.)

**Dedup: not possible from that session.** `search_issues` returned `total_count: 0` for the app's own repo even on a control term certainly present in an open issue's title, so the index was not answering. The run correctly reported these rather than filing them blind, and I am filing them with that caveat attached rather than claiming a duplicate check I did not get.

---

## Finding 1 — a key that makes the coverage report read 100% while the screen stays English

`objects.OBJECT._views.VIEW.description` is:

- **declared** by `ObjectTranslationDataSchema`,
- **walked** by the coverage extractor (it is one of the keys `os i18n check` expects),
- **authorable**, and counted as covered once authored,
- and **never read by the console.**

Two legs in one session, `zh-CN`:

| authored as | tab strip (the view **label**, one key over in the same group) | the description line under the header |
|---|---|---|
| bundle entry | 我发起的 ✅ | `Contracts I launched, grouped by where each one has got to.` ❌ |
| inline `{ en, 'zh-CN' }` map | 我发起的 ✅ | 我发起的合同，按各自进行到哪一步分组。 ✅ |

The label resolving from the *same group* is the control: the bundle is loaded, the object and view are addressed correctly, and the neighbouring key works. Only `description` is dropped on the floor.

**Why this is worse than an untranslated string.** It is a false negative in the platform's own gate. An app can author every declared key, watch `os i18n check` report zero missing, ship, and still have English descriptions on every list view in a `zh-CN` console — with no signal anywhere. The whole value of a coverage gate is that its zero means something, and this key makes the zero lie.

15 view descriptions in that app are affected. It worked around them with inline maps **and kept the bundle entries**, so a fixed resolver wins over the map and the duplication unwinds itself — but the next app will not know to do that.

---

## Finding 2 — `pages.NAME.components.*` addresses nothing on a `kind: 'slotted'` page, and a tab label has no key on any page kind

```js
let n = 0;
walkAddressedPageComponents(ContractDetailPage, (c) => (n++, c));   // -> 0
```

against **21 authored components and tab labels** (`@objectstack/spec` 17.3.0). `walkAddressedPageComponents` is the traversal `translatePage` itself runs, so this is unresolvable rather than merely ungated.

Two independent causes, either sufficient on its own:

- its roots are `regions[].components[]`, and a **slotted** page authors `slots`;
- its descent is `properties.children`, and a `page:tabs` carries `properties.items[].children`.

⇒ `pages.contract_detail` carries exactly two addressable keys, `label` and `description`, while **7 tab labels, 7 path stages, 7 related-list titles and 1 block label** cannot be reached from a bundle at all. Worked around with 22 inline locale maps.

## Finding 3 — `dashboards.NAME` has no group for `globalFilters`

The group is `label` · `description` · `actions` · `widgets`. A dashboard's global-filter labels and their option labels are not addressable — and the filter bar draws **directly above** the widget titles the bundle does translate, so the mixed-language result is maximally visible:

```
类别: 全部        Requesting Department: 全部
[six Chinese widget titles below]
```

5 filter labels + 29 option labels in that app. Worked around with inline maps.

## Finding 4 — chart category labels from `select` options ignore the bundle on same-object dimensions, and there is no workaround

On dataset-backed charts, category and series labels drawn from a `select` field's option values render the **inline English** option label, while the identical values render the translation in the list grid on the same console.

The correlation is exact and is the useful part:

| dataset dimension | declared as | renders |
|---|---|---|
| `contract_metrics.direction` | `field: 'direction'` (same object) | `Purchase` / `Sales` ❌ |
| `payment_metrics.direction` | `field: 'contract.direction'` (dotted, cross-object) | 采购 / 销售 ✅ |

Same option values, same console, same session. Also affects a `status` funnel (`Draft/Submitted/In Review/…`) and a `currency_code` bar (`EUR — Euro`).

A widget has **no authoring surface for category labels**, so unlike 1–3 this one cannot be worked around. It is the residue left visible on two of that app's three dashboards.

---

## Also worth knowing, not a finding

- `authorWarnedTranslationGroups()` returns exactly `['flows']` on spec 17.3.0, so flow screen copy is skipped by the extractor by design and is **not translatable today**. An app cannot gate on it; ours states that rather than trimming its requirement to fit.
- The coverage extractor emits `objects.OBJECT._actions.*` twice (once via `config.actions`, once via the object), so `os lint` reported 793 `i18n/missing-*` rows for 752 distinct keys. Cosmetic double-count.
- In a `zh-CN` console the Studio metadata-type list renders **`Dataset`** untranslated while every sibling type is translated (对象/视图/操作/仪表板/流程/页面/岗位/权限集/钩子). That is the `metadataForm` baseline the platform packages own, not an app string.

## Boundaries

- One app, one console build, one dialect. Re-confirm before acting.
- ⛔ Nothing was patched in the platform; findings 1–3 are worked around with inline `{ en, 'zh-CN' }` maps documented at each site, and finding 4 is left visible.
- Finding 1 is the one with a gate consequence. If only one of these is picked up, it should be that one.
